alternatives.cost: Already in the repo; would need a CLI shim to be callable outside a hook payload.
alternatives.covers: The DENY half of `gate`: pattern-based refusal of destructive commands (force push, hard reset, recursive deletion, piped-to-shell). Same deny-list discipline.
alternatives.gap: It is a PreToolUse hook for interactive Claude Code sessions and cannot be invoked by a headless worker; it has no NEEDS_AUTH tier, writes no ledger, and covers none of intent, panel, evidence or handoff. Adopting it would still leave five of the six commands to build.
alternatives.maturity: In-repo, maintained, with its own corpus and bench.
alternatives.name: hookgate (this repo, tools/hookgate, Rust)

alternatives.cost: Zero install; needs the payload-shape adaptation that worker_wrap.py already performs.
alternatives.covers: Risk-verb blocking with an explicit authorization path (LOOP_MAY_ACT_AUTHORIZED=1), which `gate` mirrors as WORKER_AUTHORIZED=1.
alternatives.gap: Documented in its own header as PAYLOAD ONLY, NOT WIRED: it reads a hook payload shape a cron worker never produces. No ledger, no intent, no panel, no evidence, no stop gate.

alternatives.cost: New infrastructure, new operational burden, vendor or self-hosted server.
alternatives.covers: Durable workflow execution with persistent state, retries and timers: the industrial answer to 'a worker that survives restarts'.
alternatives.gap: Requires a server cluster and an SDK rewrite of every worker; the workers here are plain prompts run by cron, and the requirement is a thin inheritance layer, not a workflow engine. Orders of magnitude heavier than the problem.

alternatives.cost: Zero new install where Actions already run; unusable for local cron workers.
alternatives.covers: A handoff-ish surface: each run can publish a summary and artifacts the next run downloads.
alternatives.gap: Tied to CI runs, not to cron workers on this machine; no pre-action risk gate, no intent capture, no deterministic panel over the diff, no evidence model for claims. Covers only the handoff sixth of the loop.

alternatives.cost: New dependency and framework lock-in for every worker.
alternatives.covers: Durable per-thread state for agent graphs, including replay from a checkpoint.
alternatives.gap: Requires adopting the LangGraph framework for the workers themselves; the workers are framework-free prompts. Checkpointing also covers only state, not the risk gate, panel, evidence or stop-checklist thirds.
alternatives.maturity: Mature OSS. Rejected on fit: the task is inheriting this repo's own lifecycle, not adopting a graph runtime.
alternatives.name: LangGraph checkpointing

why: worker_wrap.py maps the seven settings.json lifecycle events onto commands a headless cron worker invokes itself (begin/gate/panel/check-evidence/end), because no hook fires outside an interactive session. The value is not in any single command, all of which exist in narrower forms, but in the closed loop: intent capture, risk gate, deterministic review, evidence validation, stop checklist and hash-chained handoff in one invocable surface with one state directory. Splitting it across adopted tools would leave the worker to reimplement exactly the composition that is the point.
